ordinaryBSTW.title: Two-variable zeta elements over imaginary quadratic fields (ordinary case)

ownerRecord.target: Ordinary BSTW two-variable zeta element, both normalized explicit reciprocity laws, ordinary Perrin-Riou/Greenberg characteristic-ideal identity and equivalence in both directions, and its two-form product

hypotheses: E/Q of conductor N, p not dividing 2N good ordinary; fixed p-adic embedding and p=v*vbar split in the imaginary quadratic L; gcd(D_L,N)=1.

For the stated ordinary construction require E[p](L)=0, with the actual stable Tate lattice and source dual/Tate-twist conventions. Do not use Remark 1.15's unspecified modified reciprocity laws to erase this condition.

Use Lambda_L and its completed unramified coefficient extension separately. For general elliptic-newform comparisons retain the coefficient ring O_lambda and van_L: residual lattice invariants under G_L vanish; without van_L compare only after inverting p.

For a cyclotomic quotient require nv: both localized projected zeta classes are non-torsion over the rational cyclotomic Iwasawa algebra. This is not implied by two-variable nonvanishing or by good ordinary reduction.
BCS Theorem 4.1.3 additionally retains its elliptic-newform, split-field, discriminant and irreducibility-over-K hypotheses; Corollary 4.1.4 checks them for both forms.
ordinaryBSTW.construction: Construct the ordinary two-variable class from actual Beilinson-Kato classes varied in the CM family (BSTW Theorem 1.14 and sections 3-5). Its localization at vbar belongs to the image of ordinary H^1 for T^+(1); at v impose the source's relaxed condition. The class is not defined by demanding predicted regulator images. Build the two local maps and compare the same class, lattice, twists, periods, Euler factors and normalization with both separately constructed analytic functions.
outputs: The constructed Z(E/L), with Col_v(loc_v Z)=L_p(E/L) and Log_vbar(loc_vbar Z)=L_Gr(E/L), in the exact source coefficient rings after the stated normalization and scalar extension.
Rank-one torsion-free H_rel,ord and nonzero Z; exact Poitou-Tate sequences (9.11)-(9.13), including the map images/local correction terms needed for the normalized sequences (9.12)-(9.13).

Under the qualified two-variable hypotheses, ch(X_Gr)*(L_PR)=ch(X_ord)*(L_Gr) in the completed unramified Iwasawa ring, integrally under van_L and p-inverted otherwise. Prove torsion before writing these characteristic ideals; retain the common strict-Selmer correction term in both sequence calculations until cancellation is justified.

Equivalence of either oriented one-sided divisibility, and the direct-sum two-form product identity of BCS Theorem 4.1.3/Corollary 4.1.4. For cyclotomic versions use nv; do not assert unrestricted anticyclotomic equivalence or signed construction.
ordinaryBSTW.proofOutline: Compute ch(H/Lambda Z)*ch(X_Gr)=(L_Gr)*ch(X_st) and ch(H/Lambda Z)*ch(X_ord)=(L_PR)*ch(X_st) from the two four-term exact sequences, after common unramified scalar extension. Use proved rank, nonvanishing and torsion to cancel only nonzero characteristic ideals. This supplies the ordinary comparison once; the product follows by direct sums/multiplicativity.
api: Constructed-class and localization maps with ordinary local-condition landing, scalar-extension/weight-specialization squares in the proven range.
Two regulator reciprocity theorems on the same normalized class; change-of-basis/period unit covariance and coefficient-ring transport.
Exact-sequence characteristic-ideal identities retaining H/Lambda Z and X_st; ordinary comparison in both orientations and multiplicative two-form version.
tests: Recover weight-two Kato specialization on the same lattice; test a unit period/basis change and an isogeny factor that is not a unit.
Check both containment orientations and the two-form product without asserting equality of arbitrarily normalized analytic elements.
Keep van_L=false comparisons p-inverted; do not infer integral equality from rational equality.
Check a vanishing projected localization: nv fails, so the cyclotomic comparison cannot be exported by the two-variable theorem.
Retain nonzero H/Lambda Z and strict-Selmer correction terms in a four-term-sequence example; they are not assumed trivial.
Reject an ordinary import as a proof of either signed supersingular reciprocity law.
